title: One open support operation preserves the system bounds
statement: Fix a finite-field datum D, a prime l different from its characteristic, a finite extension E of Q_l and the specified strict system operations o. Let j:X to Y be a quasi-compact open immersion of schemes of finite type over Spec D.k, without separatedness hypotheses on their structure morphisms. For every Good system M on X and every derived-complete bounded constructible integral K on X, the specified system extension by zero of M is Good on Y, and the localized completed-ring extension by zero of K is integral constructible on Y. The two assertions are independent; they require no relation between M and K.

proof.text: Apply finiteStageDerivedExtensionByZero_constructibleFiniteTor at every positive coefficient level. It preserves the same support and Tor intervals. Transport constructibility, support and Tor amplitude through the specified open evaluation isomorphism.

Use the canonical ambient model to obtain a realization model for canonical operations. The proved fixedOpenReduction_isIso helper of open reconstruction effectivity gives an invertible open-reduction mate on every integral object. Normalized reconstruction identifies M with reduction of its actual total limit by the invertible counit. Applying open extension and the open-reduction mate therefore identifies its output with a reduction system, hence normalized. Uniqueness of left adjoints to the fixed system pullback identifies the canonical open functor with o.extension. Transport normalization through this whole-system isomorphism.

Rebuild compatible etale origins from the output level bounds. Convert each intrinsic level by the canonical finite-module equivalence and use bounded constructible etale descent. Transfer each actual system transition to the fixed coefficient level via full faithfulness, then lift its etale comparison through the bounded-below fully faithful site comparison. The two required squares follow by cancelling the chosen comparison isomorphisms.

For the independent integral clause, use the constructibility component of the already constructed canonical open-factor coherence data for j. Its extension functor is exactly ringedOpen. Combine this with output normalization, bounds and origins to obtain both original conclusions.

proof_origin.place: B3: reuse proved finite open CTF bounds and canonical open-factor integral preservation; reconstruct origins by etale descent; prove normalization through the invertible actual reconstruction counit and canonical open-reduction mate.

theorem openSupportStep_bounds (D : FiniteFieldDatum.{u}) (hl : l ≠ D.p)
    (o : Operations l E) {X Y : Over (Spec (CommRingCat.of D.k))}
    [LocallyOfFiniteType X.hom] [QuasiCompact X.hom]
    [LocallyOfFiniteType Y.hom] [QuasiCompact Y.hom]
    (j : X ⟶ Y) [IsOpenImmersion j.left] [QuasiCompact j.left]
    (M : System l E X.left) (hM : Good l E X.left M) (K : Integral l E X.left)
    (hK : sfIntegralConstructible l E X.left K) :
    Good l E Y.left ((Operations.shriek l E o j.left).obj M) ∧
      sfIntegralConstructible l E Y.left ((ringedOpen l E j.left).obj K)
